Methods / numerical checks · integrated 17 October 2026

What the radiation calculation has—and has not—been checked against

Numerically benchmarked on specified cases. Not field validated.
These results compare calculations using synthetic weather and idealized geometry. They do not establish prediction accuracy for a real site, compliance, or suitability for research conclusions.

Independent calculation reference

pvlib 0.13.1 supplies NREL SPA geometric solar positions and isotropic sky transposition. FORM uses the corrected NOAA/Meeus Julian-century solar position. Both exclude ground reflection. We use 12 city/date scenarios: Cairo, Berlin, Riyadh and Sydney on 20 March, 21 June and 21 December 2026, with six surface orientations and 1- and 5-minute integration.

Weather inputs are synthetic hourly DNI and DHI, held constant within each hour. This deliberately isolates the calculation from weather-provider accuracy. The fixed UTC offsets are scenario settings, not automatic civil time zones.

CheckObserved result

Regression gate chosen for these cases: absolute difference ≤ max(0.02 kWh/m², 2% of reference daily total). This is a project engineering tolerance, not a standard or certification. Absolute and relative maxima can occur in different cases.

Time-step sensitivity and the correction

The earlier 30-minute method differed from the same-step pvlib reference by 10.93% in one Berlin east-facing equinox case. Near-horizon visibility changes can amplify small solar-position differences. The integrated version corrects solar geometry and retains the 5-minute cap, with a selectable 1-minute convergence check; the weather remains hourly and no finer weather information is implied.

Geometry stepLargest change from FORM 1-minute calculation

These are sensitivity measurements, not error bounds for other designs. Thin obstructions and moving shadow boundaries require further convergence checks.

Sky-obstruction check

Four probes around a 10 × 20 × 10 m box are compared against a separate Python ray/axis-aligned-box implementation using 131,072 sky directions. FORM uses triangle intersections with 2,048 sky directions by default; 512 and 8,192 remain selectable. The frozen box reference uses the original 20 mm offset; FORM now uses 0.1 mm, and separate finite-obstacle quadrature fixtures verify this correction. The reference itself is a numerical approximation.

Remaining validation work

  • Compare measured or independently simulated irradiation on realistic façades, courtyards, setbacks and overhangs.
  • Quantify sensitivity to surface sampling, sky resolution and shadow time steps for each design type.
  • Evaluate hourly DNI/GHI/DHI consistency, low-sun reconstruction and weather-grid uncertainty.
  • Compare an anisotropic sky model and quantify omitted ground and building reflections.
  • Check browser interaction and exported results end to end.

FORM still excludes ground reflection, interreflection, glazing transmission and PV conversion. A daylight or indoor comfort claim is not supported by these checks.

Daylight and sky-exposure checks

Façade Vertical Sky Component (VSC) uses an outward-facing virtual vertical receiver and the CIE standard overcast distribution L = 1 + 2 sin(altitude). The reference horizontal illuminance is 7π/3 in relative units. It excludes reflected light. Sky-view factor instead uses a horizontal receiver with cosine weighting; visible-sky solid-angle percentage is a third, separate quantity.

These are idealized tests, not validation against measured buildings. No room illuminance or regulatory pass/fail outcome is provided.

Audit integration

The original 144-case benchmark is retained alongside the audit’s 60 surface cases, three independent finite-obstacle view factors and nine shaded scenes at five time resolutions. Coarse-step tables intentionally override the production cap to characterize numerical sensitivity. Read the integration report for scope and remaining checks. These are numerical experiments, not measured building accuracy.

Reproduce and inspect

Download detailed benchmark results (JSON) · Source repository

Run npm run validate:radiation and npm test. Regenerate the independent fixture with python scripts/generate-radiation-reference.py after installing pvlib==0.13.1. The generator imports no FORM calculation functions.
